# Knowledge Base Metadata

Filter when searching a Knowledge Base

Metadata is additional information attached to your Knowledge Base files that you can filter on when searching, similar to filtering columns in a spreadsheet.

## Types of Metadata

### Standard Metadata

Automatically inherited from the source (file name, source URL, upload date, etc.). Standard metadata is read-only. To update it, make changes at the source and re-sync.

### Custom Metadata

Tag Knowledge Base files with your own key-value pairs to organize and filter content by dimensions like Region, Product, Audience, or Content Type. [...] Last updated

## Adding Metadata

### Custom Metadata (UI)

1. Click any file in your Knowledge Base to open its details
2. In the Custom Metadata section, click Add
3. Enter a Key (e.g., "country") and Value (e.g., "France")
4. Click Save Changes

### CSV / Google Sheets

When uploading a CSV or Google Sheet, all columns are stored as metadata. You can choose which columns are searchable. The rest are still returned as metadata but can only be used for filtering.

### Other Methods

 API - Use the Knowledge Bases API "Update" endpoint
 Workflow - Use the "Knowledge Base Write" Step

## Filtering with Metadata

### SEO-Optimized Knowledge Base Content

Digital knowledge bases can help generate organic traffic and boost the results rankings of your documents. To do this, the content hub must be optimized for search engines like Google and Bing. With features like custom metadata options, your knowledge base will help search engine bots crawl and index your content.

### AI-Powered Support Assistant

Enhance knowledge base search tools with Generative AI (GenAI) to turn a normal quest for information into a conversational experience. Users enter their questions in natural language into a self-service chatbot or search bar interface and automatically receive accurate responses. [...] Documentation trends: Identify the most popular content and search terms to prioritize content work. Look at the least-read content to discover which topics aren’t as critical for users.  Are they less popular due to a lack of questions on the topic or because users search for different keywords?
 Content findability: With keyword analytics, see what customers search for. If they use different terms than those in the content, enhance your knowledge base with new metadata, taxonomies, and synonyms. This will improve your content findability and usefulness.
 No-results searches: Identify content gaps with “Searches with no results”. When results are lacking, documentation teams need to produce or update content. [...] Cover of KMWorld Report AI

Knowledge Base FAQs

Teams should organize content in a knowledge base around the questions and tasks users need to complete, using clear categories, metadata, navigation, and search. Regular content audits and updates are also important for keeping information easy to find and trustworthy.

Knowledge management is typically a cross-functional responsibility involving technical writers, knowledge teams, subject matter experts, support teams, product teams, and other content owners. It may also include HR and Legal if the knowledge base includes internal process information. IT may be involved in creating the hub and connecting it to different content sources. Clear ownership and review processes help ensure that information remains accurate and current.

## 3. Product Documentation Knowledge Base

Product documentation knowledge bases house technical information about how your software, application, or digital product functions. This knowledge base type is fundamentally different from general support content. It focuses on product-specific technical details rather than company policies or broad customer service topics. ## 1. Customer-Facing Knowledge Base Platforms

Customer-facing knowledge base platforms function as public self-service portals where customers access information about your products and services without restrictions. These external types of knowledge bases remain available to anyone seeking answers, unlike internal systems reserved for employees. You’ll find them embedded on company websites, within products, or hosted at dedicated domains like support.company.com. [...] ## 7. Community-Driven or Collaborative Knowledge Base

High levels of community engagement and collaboration see a 10% increase in customer loyalty. Many organizations are shifting toward a collaborative model in which users contribute to the documentation. This type functions as a peer-to-peer repository where long-time customers or power users share workarounds, creative use cases, and localized solutions that a corporate team might miss.

Crowdsourcing information ensures that the library remains dynamic and reflects real-world applications. Moderation tools allow your staff to verify community answers, turning a simple forum into a trusted, authoritative source. This reduces the burden on your content team while fostering a sense of ownership among your most loyal brand advocates.

## Supported metadata data types

The following data types are supported for metadata attributes:

 `STRING` – A text value.
 `NUMBER` – A numeric value. When using the CSV-based metadata configuration described on this page, number values are stored as strings.
 `BOOLEAN` – A true or false value.
 `STRING_LIST` – A list of string values.

For the full metadata attribute schema used in filtering queries, see MetadataAttributeSchema in the API Reference.

## Related metadata configuration options [...] ## Related metadata configuration options

In addition to the CSV-based metadata configuration described on this page, you can also configure metadata using a sidecar `.metadata.json` file for any document type in an Amazon S3 data source. This method supports the full set of data types and the `includeForEmbedding` option. For more information, see Document metadata fields.

To learn how to filter query results using metadata, see the Knowledge base prompt templates section in Configure and customize queries and response generation.

In this example:

 `contentFields` – Specifies one column (`description`) as the content to be chunked and embedded. Only one content field is supported.
 `fieldsToInclude` – Specifies which columns (`city` and `price`) to treat as filterable metadata. The `bedrooms` column is excluded because it is not listed.
 `metadataAttributes` – Specifies document-level metadata applied to every chunk from this CSV. In this example, `source` is a static attribute applied to all rows.

Each row produces one chunk. For the first row, the chunk text is the description, and the metadata is `city: "Seattle"`, `price: "450000"`, and `source: "property_listings_2024"`. All metadata values from CSV columns are stored as strings.

When using the CSV-based metadata configuration described on this page, number values are stored as strings. `BOOLEAN` – A true or false value. `STRING_LIST` – A list of string values. For the full metadata attribute schema used in filtering queries, see MetadataAttributeSchema in the API Reference. ## Related metadata configuration options ## Related metadata configuration options In addition to the CSV-based metadata configuration described on this page, you can also configure metadata using a sidecar `.metadata.json` file for any document type in an Amazon S3 data source. This method supports the full set of data types and the `includeForEmbedding` option. For more information, see Document metadata fields. chunk_3.source: What Is a Knowledge Base? Definition, Types & Benefits
chunk_3.text: ### SEO-Optimized Knowledge Base Content Digital knowledge bases can help generate organic traffic and boost the results rankings of your documents. To do this, the content hub must be optimized for search engines like Google and Bing. With features like custom metadata options, your knowledge base will help search engine bots crawl and index your content. ### AI-Powered Support Assistant Enhance knowledge base search tools with Generative AI (GenAI) to turn a normal quest for information into a conversational experience. Users enter their questions in natural language into a self-service chatbot or search bar interface and automatically receive accurate responses. Documentation trends: Identify the most popular content and search terms to prioritize content work. Look at the least-read content to discover which topics aren’t as critical for users. Are they less popular due to a lack of questions on the topic or because users search for different keywords? Content findability: With keyword analytics, see what customers search for. If they use different terms than those in the content, enhance your knowledge base with new metadata, taxonomies, and synonyms. This will improve your content findability and usefulness. No-results searches: Identify content gaps with “Searches with no results”. When results are lacking, documentation teams need to produce or update content. Cover of KMWorld Report AI Knowledge Base FAQs Teams should organize content in a knowledge base around the questions and tasks users need to complete, using clear categories, metadata, navigation, and search. Regular content audits and updates are also important for keeping information easy to find and trustworthy. Knowledge management is typically a cross-functional responsibility involving technical writers, knowledge teams, subject matter experts, support teams, product teams, and other content owners. It may also include HR and Legal if the knowledge base includes internal process information. IT may be involved in creating the hub and connecting it to different content sources. Clear ownership and review processes help ensure that information remains accurate and current.

chunk_4.text: ###### Modernize Your Knowledge Base Replace static folders with a dynamic, searchable home for all your company data. Book a FREE Demo Enterprise Intelligence ## 3. Product Documentation Knowledge Base Product documentation knowledge bases house technical information about how your software, application, or digital product functions. This knowledge base type is fundamentally different from general support content. It focuses on product-specific technical details rather than company policies or broad customer service topics. You create reference material that explains what each feature does, how users interact with specific functionality, and technical specifications that developers need for integration. Learn More Enterprise Intelligence A list of the different types of knowledge bases ## 1. Customer-Facing Knowledge Base Platforms Customer-facing knowledge base platforms function as public self-service portals where customers access information about your products and services without restrictions. These external types of knowledge bases remain available to anyone seeking answers, unlike internal systems reserved for employees. You’ll find them embedded on company websites, within products, or hosted at dedicated domains like support.company.com. ## 7. Community-Driven or Collaborative Knowledge Base High levels of community engagement and collaboration see a 10% increase in customer loyalty. Many organizations are shifting toward a collaborative model in which users contribute to the documentation. This type functions as a peer-to-peer repository where long-time customers or power users share workarounds, creative use cases, and localized solutions that a corporate team might miss. Crowdsourcing information ensures that the library remains dynamic and reflects real-world applications. Moderation tools allow your staff to verify community answers, turning a simple forum into a trusted, authoritative source. This reduces the burden on your content team while fostering a sense of ownership among your most loyal brand advocates.
